910.name: Ancient Dilmun and Failaka
910.description: The Bronze Age settlements on Failaka Island linked to the Dilmun civilization, Mesopotamian trade routes through the Persian Gulf, and the Hellenistic outpost established by Alexander's successors.

sub_clusters.name: Bronze Age Failaka and Dilmun Trade
sub_clusters.description: Failaka Island as a key node in the Dilmun maritime network connecting Mesopotamia with the Indus Valley, temples, stamp seals, and the island's role in Gulf trade.
key_events: Dilmun-era temples and settlements flourish on Failaka Island (c. 2000 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Hellenistic Ikaros
sub_clusters.description: The Seleucid establishment of a Greek colony on Failaka, known as Ikaros, its fortress and temple, and the blending of Greek and local Gulf cultures.

910.name: Pre-Islamic and Early Islamic Kuwait
910.description: The coastal communities of the Kuwait region in the Characene and Sassanid periods, the early spread of Islam to the Gulf, and the area's role in maritime trade.

sub_clusters.name: Characene and Sassanid Gulf
sub_clusters.description: The Characene kingdom's influence on the Kuwaiti coast, Sassanid control of the Persian Gulf, the Kazima region, and early Christian communities in the Gulf.

sub_clusters.name: Islamic Conquest and Kazima
sub_clusters.description: The Battle of Chains at Kazima in the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid Empire, the region's integration into the early Caliphate, and Gulf maritime trade under Umayyad rule.
key_events: Battle of Chains (Kazima) — Khalid ibn al-Walid defeats Sassanid forces near Kuwait (633 AD)

920.name: Medieval Gulf Trade and Regional Powers
920.description: The Kuwaiti coast under Abbasid, Carmathian, and regional Gulf powers, the maritime trade linking Basra to India and East Africa, and the development of pearl diving settlements.

sub_clusters.name: Abbasid and Carmathian Period
sub_clusters.description: The Gulf coast's prosperity under the Abbasid Caliphate, the Carmathian revolt's disruption of trade, and the region's role as a waypoint for Indian Ocean commerce.

sub_clusters.name: Late Medieval Gulf Settlements
sub_clusters.description: The development of fishing and pearl-diving communities along the Kuwait coast, the influence of the Jabrid and Uyunid dynasties of eastern Arabia, and overland caravan routes.

930.name: Portuguese, Ottoman, and Early Bani Utbah
930.description: Portuguese and Ottoman competition for Gulf control, the rise of the Bani Khalid emirate, and the migration of the Bani Utbah to Kuwait founding the settlement that would become the modern state.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese and Ottoman Gulf Rivalry
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese naval domination of the Gulf, Ottoman claims to Basra and the northern Gulf, and the disruption and reshaping of traditional trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Bani Utbah Founding of Kuwait
sub_clusters.description: The earliest references to 'Kuwait' (little fort), the migration of the Bani Utbah confederation from Najd, and the establishment of Kuwait town as a trading and pearl-diving center.
key_events: Earliest known reference to the settlement of Kuwait (Qurain/Grane) (c. 1613)
The Al-Sabah family assumes leadership of Kuwait (1752)

930.name: Al-Sabah Dynasty and Early Statehood
930.description: The consolidation of Al-Sabah rule, Kuwait's emergence as a major Gulf trading port, the pearl industry's peak, and the strategic maneuvering between Ottoman and British interests.

sub_clusters.name: Kuwait as Trading Hub
sub_clusters.description: Kuwait's growth into one of the premier merchant ports of the Gulf, the dhow-building industry, extensive pearl-diving fleets, and trade links to India, East Africa, and the Ottoman interior.

sub_clusters.name: Mubarak the Great and British Alliance
sub_clusters.description: Sheikh Mubarak al-Sabah's seizure of power, the Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement of 1899 establishing a British protectorate, and the strategic balancing against Ottoman encroachment.
key_events: Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement makes Kuwait a British protectorate (1899)

940.name: British Protectorate and Oil Discovery
940.description: Kuwait under British protection, the decline of the pearl industry, the transformative discovery of oil at Burgan field, and the rapid modernization leading to independence.

sub_clusters.name: Decline of Pearling and Oil Concessions
sub_clusters.description: The collapse of the pearl market due to Japanese cultured pearls, the 1934 Kuwait Oil Company concession, the discovery of the massive Burgan oil field, and WWII disruptions.
key_events: Oil discovered at Burgan field — one of the world's largest (1938)
First commercial oil export from Kuwait (1946)

sub_clusters.name: Oil Wealth and Independence
sub_clusters.description: The extraordinary transformation from a small trading port to one of the world's wealthiest states, massive infrastructure development, and the achievement of full independence from Britain.
key_events: Iraq immediately claims Kuwait; British troops deter invasion (1961)

950.name: Modern Kuwait and Souk al-Manakh Crisis
950.description: The development of Kuwait's welfare state, the nationalization of the oil industry, the catastrophic Souk al-Manakh stock market crash, and the Iran-Iraq War's impact on Gulf security.

sub_clusters.name: Welfare State and Oil Nationalization
sub_clusters.description: The creation of a comprehensive welfare state, the establishment of the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development, and the full nationalization of the Kuwait Oil Company.

sub_clusters.name: Souk al-Manakh and Gulf Tensions
sub_clusters.description: The 1982 Souk al-Manakh stock market crash devastating the economy, the tanker war during the Iran-Iraq conflict, and Kuwait's reflagging of tankers under the US flag.
key_events: Souk al-Manakh stock market crash — $94 billion in post-dated checks (1982)

950.name: Iraqi Invasion and Liberation
950.description: Saddam Hussein's invasion and brutal occupation of Kuwait, the international coalition assembled under Operation Desert Shield/Storm, and the liberation of Kuwait.

sub_clusters.name: Iraqi Invasion and Occupation
sub_clusters.description: Iraq's invasion on August 2, 1990, the seven-month occupation marked by looting, torture, and the attempt to annex Kuwait as Iraq's 19th province.
key_events: UN Security Council Resolution 678 authorizes use of force (November 1990)

sub_clusters.name: Operation Desert Storm and Liberation
sub_clusters.description: The US-led coalition's air campaign and 100-hour ground war, the retreating Iraqi army's destruction of over 700 oil wells, and Kuwait's liberation on February 26, 1991.
key_events: Coalition ground offensive liberates Kuwait in 100 hours (February 1991)
Iraqi forces set fire to over 700 Kuwaiti oil wells during retreat (1991)

960.name: Post-Liberation Reconstruction and Modernization
960.description: Kuwait's reconstruction from wartime devastation, democratic developments in the National Assembly, economic diversification efforts under Kuwait Vision 2035, and regional security challenges.

sub_clusters.name: Reconstruction and Democratic Expansion
sub_clusters.description: The massive post-war reconstruction effort, extinguishing of oil fires, women's suffrage in 2005, and the ongoing tensions between the elected National Assembly and the ruling family.
key_events: Kuwaiti women granted the right to vote and run for office (2005)

sub_clusters.name: Vision 2035 and Contemporary Kuwait
sub_clusters.description: The New Kuwait Vision 2035 diversification strategy, recurring parliamentary crises, the impact of the Arab Spring, oil price fluctuations, and Kuwait's mediating role in the Gulf diplomatic crisis.
key_events: Kuwait mediates the Qatar-Gulf diplomatic crisis (2017–2021)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
